title: Autoscaler Circuit Breaker with Adaptive Tenant Quotas
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Implement a resilient circuit-breaker layer that sits between the autoscaler and admission controller to protect fleet SLOs when predictive scaling misses demand spikes. The feature adapts per-tenant soft quotas and exposes graceful degradation strategies (queued retries, best-effort throughput, temporary shedding) while coordinating with the autoscaler to avoid thrashing and expensive overprovisioning.

Why: We observe two classes of incidents: (1) sudden tenant-driven spikes that exceed reserved capacity, and (2) autoscaler lag where scale-up is delayed by provisioning time. Both lead to high tail latency and SLA violations. A fast-acting local circuit breaker can absorb short bursts without requiring permanent capacity commits and can signal the autoscaler to accelerate or to hold.

Scope: Proof-of-concept in a single dedicated pool type (g4dn-like) for tenant-scoped fleets, with a config model for soft quota, burst pool size, and degrade policy. Deliverables include admission-side algorithm, autoscaler API changes to accept circuit signals, control-plane dashboard metrics, and an integration test harness.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Circuit-breaker accepts tenant config and emits metrics (tripped, allowance, dropped_reqs) visible in Console and Prometheus.
2) When a spike occurs that exceeds soft quota, circuit chooses between: a short-queue with headroom, best-effort pass-through, or shedding according to tenant policy.
3) Autoscaler receives hint and reacts (accelerate vs hold) without flip-flopping for at least the configured stabilization window.
4) E2E test simulating spike shows <5% error increase and latency degradation contained to configured SLO window vs baseline.
5) No regression on non-dedicated shared pools (smoke tests pass).
steps: Design: finalize flow diagram and state machine for circuit (closed, open, half-open, cooling) — include burst pooling semantics
Control-plane: extend tenant config model with soft_quota, burst_pool, priority_degrade_strategy
Admission-side: implement fast-path quota check with token-bucket + short local queue and async shed decision
Autoscaler integration: define API to accept circuit hints (urgency, sustained_load_estimate) and a backoff policy to avoid oscillation
Metrics & observability: expose granular metrics, tracing points, and a Console panel for affected tenants
Testing: chaos tests (node loss, large spike), regression tests, and perf benchmarks of added admission latency
Rollout: gated canary in a single region, monitor dashboards for 72 hours, then widen to more pools
updates: 2025-02-12 - Ticket created by Aisha: initial proposal and problem statement. Linked to ENG-20641 (autoscaler workstream).
2025-02-14 - Design review with PM/Runtime team: agreed on token-bucket + short queue hybrid and three degrade strategies (queue, best-effort, shed). Diego to prototype admission fast-path.
2025-02-16 - Prototype: implemented local token-bucket and short FIFO queue in admission layer; microbenchmarks show 0.45ms median added latency. PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/4812

2025-02-18 - Feedback from Reliability: requested explicit stabilization window and circuit hysteresis to avoid autoscaler thrash. Added fields: stabilization_seconds and hysteresis_factor. Decided to emit 'urgency' hint levels (low/medium/high).
2025-02-20 - Integration work started: autoscaler API patch in progress (github.com/redwood/autoscaler/pull/223). Working through auth for control-plane hints and rate-limit of hint traffic.

2025-02-22 - Blocker identified: burst_pool accounting across replicas requires a consistent reservoir view. Exploring two approaches: (A) centralized burst service (strong consistency) or (B) probabilistic local reservoirs with occasional reconciliation. PM prefers B for lower latency; engineering wants A for correctness. Providence meeting scheduled 2025-02-24.
notes: Trade-offs considered: centralized reservoir provides strict burst guarantees at cost of additional RPCs and single-point-of-failure; local reservoirs reduce RPCs but can overcommit. We'll prototype local reservoirs with a reconciliation protocol and fall back to centralized if we see >2% overcommit in chaos tests.

Rollout plan: start with non-critical tenants on dedicated pools that are flagged as experimental. Ensure easy kill switch via feature flag and default to existing admission logic if the feature fails.
Security: no new customer data is stored; hints are telemetry only. Security review not required but audit logs will be included for autoscaler hint endpoints.
